title: Indore Edible Oils & Vanaspati: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Crushing and refining is a spread business, not a brand business at the small end: you buy soybean or mustard seed, crush, refine, and sell oil plus de-oiled cake. **Cash is made on the crush spread and lost on inventory timing.** Margins are thin — a rated peer ran PBILDT of 1.47% to 3.32% across FY15-FY17 on low value addition and fragmented competition [9]. So when a proposal lands, check the gross spread per tonne and the hedging policy before you look at turnover; if there is no hedge, ask who bears a price fall and get it in writing.

## Where value and cash sit now
Value sits with branded packers and with anyone who can hold stock cheaply; cash sits in working capital, because seed must be bought at harvest and oil sold through the year. **Raw material is the largest cost line and its volatility is the core credit risk** [8][10]. Local demand is shifting: soybean refined oil demand is reported surging in Indore as mustard prices retreat [1], which helps refiners' volumes but squeezes the spread. Note the source is a single local report dated 30-Oct-2026 [1].

## What has changed, and what is local noise
Three things are real. MP GST collections are -0.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1% [D] — a genuine local demand signal. India bank credit is +45.5% YoY against output +5.1% [D], so the system is lending far ahead of production; expect over-levered borrowers in this trade. Repo is 5.5% and tightening [D], which raises the cost of carrying inventory. Against that, the Indore soy conclave pushed for a stable 10-year import policy and doubled soybean yields [3] — that is advocacy, not policy. Adulteration seizures of 341 kg in Indore [2] are an enforcement story, not a demand story, but they do flag weak quality controls at small units.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue branded refiners and vanaspati units with own distribution, hedged books and leverage under control.** Peer results show the model works: AWL Agri grew revenue 18% YoY to Rs 21,465 crore on 14% volume growth with EBITDA up 40% [5][6], though its Q2FY26 EBIT fell 13% on a 22% revenue rise [4] — proof that volume growth alone does not protect margin. **Avoid unbranded crushers, traders funding stock on cash credit, and anyone whose sales grew while GST in the state went negative.**

## How to grow safely
Structure as a cash-flow loan against a drawing-power limit computed on stock and receivables, not on turnover. Take monthly stock statements, hedged-position reports and spread-per-tonne; take quarterly CMA and GST returns. **If the borrower cannot show a hedge on more than half of open inventory, cut the limit.**

## Early warning signs
- Stock statements showing inventory days rising while sales are flat -> freeze the limit and inspect godowns.
- GST returns diverging from bank turnover -> ask for the reconciliation before the next disbursement.
- Any interest payment delay, however technical — a peer had a Rs 65 lakh delay on a working capital demand loan [11] — treat it as a signal, not an accident.
watch: Inventory days up two months running -> freeze limit, inspect godown
Unhedged inventory above half of stock -> cut limit, demand hedge
Quarterly GST returns vs bank turnover
Divergence above 10% -> stop disbursement, seek reconciliation
Any delay, even one day -> escalate, reprice or exit
MP GST stays negative two quarters -> shift to branded-only book
